{{short description|Canadian mathematician}}
'''Sally Patricia Cockburn''' (born 1960){{r|born}} is a mathematician whose research ranges from [[algebraic topology]] and [[set theory]] to [[geometric graph theory]] and [[combinatorial optimization]].  A Canadian immigrant to the US, she is William R. Kenan Jr. Professor of Mathematics at [[Hamilton College]], and former chair of the mathematics department at Hamilton.{{r|3pro|profile}}

==Education and career==
Cockburn is originally from [[Ottawa]]. She earned a bachelor's and master's degree from [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in [[Ontario]], in 1982 and 1984 respectively,{{r|socks}} and also has a master's degree from the [[University of Ottawa]].{{r|profile}} 

Following receipt of her master's degree, she taught math at a [[Maru-a-Pula_School]], a private secondary school in [[Gaborone]], [[Botswana]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.queensu.ca/mathstat/sites/mastwww/files/uploaded_files/department/communicator/13_QMathCommunicatorDecember1986.pdf|format=PDF|title=Queen's Mathematical Communicator|date=December 1986|website=Queensu.ca|access-date=2026-07-12}}</ref>

She completed her Ph.D. in algebraic topology in 1991 from [[Yale University]]. Her dissertation, ''The Gamma-Filtration on Extra-Special <math>P</math>-Groups'', was supervised by Ronnie Lee.{{r|mgp}}

She joined the Hamilton College faculty in 1991 and was promoted to full professor in 2014.{{r|3pro}} At Hamilton, she has also served as the coach for the college's [[Squash (sport)|squash]] team.{{r|socks}}

==Recognition==
Cockburn won the 2014 [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] with Joshua Lesperance for their joint work, "deranged socks", on a variation of the problem of counting [[derangement]]s.{{r|socks|mmcba}}
